title: Representative-normalized scalar global derived Hom
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a small ringed site, with commutative ring sheaf $R$, external commutative ring $A$, and specified $s:A\to\Gamma(R)$. Use the scalar-valued sections and their right derivation $G_{R,A,s}$ [def-sfb-ringed-site-scalar-global-sections], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define scalar-valued global derived Hom to be $\mathrm{GH}_{R,A,s}(K,L)=G_{R,A,s}(R\mathcal Hom_R(K,L))$ using the recorded internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. A normalized global-Hom identification consists of natural additive equivalences $H^n\mathrm{GH}_{R,A,s}(K,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,L[n])$ for all integers $n$, normalized on a K-flat complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] and arbitrary $M$ as follows. Use the actual fixed K-injective replacement $I(M)$, internal-Hom localization factorization, inverse localized augmentation and product projections [def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation]. A cycle of $\Gamma_{R,A,s}\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,I(M))$ represents the unique external Hom cocycle whose components are the module maps corresponding to its product-projection sections. Under the derived-sections computation map and inverse internal-Hom representative factorization, its cohomology class must map to the localization of that cocycle's shifted chain map, followed by the inverse localized augmentation and the canonical shift comparisons. This defines the normalization condition; it does not assert that such equivalences exist. For closed tensor-Hom data $S$ and its canonical K-flat model [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model], its ringed tensor corner [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-square-presentation] has the same site, ring, derived category and $S$'s tensor. The corner's representative model is the restriction of that K-flat comparison to the full subcategory of K-flat complexes whose terms are flat; no new tensor or comparison is chosen.
